bench-and-bill.sentence: The Aviation Operations Board on Thursday approved Kestrel Aerial's drone delivery service.
Under the approval, a single pilot can oversee up to 20 drones at once.
Flights are allowed only between sunrise and sunset.
Kestrel must report any crash or injury to the board within 24 hours.
The approval lasts 2 years, after which Kestrel will have to apply again.

byteward.sentence: Kestrel Aerial has won approval from the Aviation Operations Board to deliver packages by drone.
Kestrel will launch first in the suburbs of Phoenix and Dallas.
The drones will only fly during daylight.

launch-desk.sentence: Kestrel Aerial is cleared to start drone deliveries.
The first orders fly on December 1.
Grocery chain Pantryfield is Kestrel's first retail partner.
Kestrel raised $180 million from investors in May.

ohm-and-bit.sentence: Kestrel Aerial now has approval to run drone deliveries.
Kestrel's drones carry packages of up to 5 pounds.
They have a round-trip range of 12 miles.
Instead of landing, each drone hovers at 80 feet and lowers the package on a tether.
One pilot can supervise as many as 20 of them at a time.
To make that safe, each drone carries a small radar that spots other aircraft on its own.
